Neither is taken: 8:15 only points forward to what 8:16 then shows and 8:17 puts the same question to the same tableau, so each carries the tour on instead of opening a unit, and a cut at either would leave a row under three verses that is no complete word-event unit.
P02-003.strongest_rejected_alternative: The live rival is a seam at 8:15/8:16, weighed here face by face and held. Its far face is the pointer close at oshb:Ezek.8.15, the third of this tour's forward-pointing 'you will again see' transitions (8:6, 8:13, 8:15); its near face, the candidate onset, is oshb:Ezek.8.16, a transport verse of the counted class (sweep: 33 verses) and one of this vision's scene seams: this witness carries a said-to-me verse at 8:5 and transports at 8:7, 8:14 and 8:16. The rival is therefore licensed on its near face and one-faced, and it is not dismissed. The row holds because a licensed driver yields a row under three verses only when it is a complete word-event unit: a cut before 8:16 leaves 8:14-8:15, which MEASURED on the WEB face is only 2 verses (the remainder 8:16-8:18 has 3) and is not a complete word-event unit. The samekh recorded on MT 8:14 (single-witness) is entered as support for the alternative it favours and no wider: a mark is recorded on the verse it stands after, so honouring it as a close would end this row at its own onset verse, 8:14, a one-verse row that is no complete word-event unit, and a section break carries corroborating weight only, ranking below every licensed driver.

The righteous grandson's case (18:14) and the summary restatement (18:19-20) follow without any fresh formula onset of their own, since 18:18 explicitly recalls the father's own guilt from 18:10-13 before drawing the general rule -- one continuous legal argument across three generations, not three independently onset units. That pair of seams is the ground on which this row's confidence is held down.

The row continues through the singers' and priests' chambers (40:44-46, including the Zadokite priestly qualification, case-law texture inside a measurement row, disclosed) and closes at 40:47's וְהַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לִפְנֵ֥י הַבָּֽיִת (oshb:Ezek.40.47) “The altar was before the house” (web:Ezek.40.47), a summary notice before 40:48's transport verb moves the tour into the temple building itself. Both sides of this row are held to a lower confidence than its neighbors precisely because neither its onset nor its close carries a counted formula device.
P10-005.device_notes: No parashah, K/Q or editorial note touches 40:38-40:47. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: two occurrences (40:43, 40:47). Content disclosure, not a category deviation: 40:44-46 carries priestly-qualification (Zadokite) texture that reads closer to temple law than to measurement; the row is classed in the temple-measurement category because dimensioned description dominates it (tables, hooks, court) and the qualification clause is two verses inside a ten-verse row. A licensed rival stands inside the row at 40:44/40:45, where oshb:Ezek.40.45 opens וַיְדַבֵּ֖ר אֵלָ֑י - the guide speaking to the prophet inside the vision, which carries an onset here. It is weighed and not taken, because that speech names the chambers 40:44 has just described and opens no new measured object.

P10-011.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:15 opens וְכִלָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.42.15) “when he had finished measuring the inner house” (web:Ezek.42.15) -- a completion notice, not a counted formula, pressed into onset service here, since it explicitly marks the end of the inner-house survey that has run since 40:5 before turning outward to the perimeter wall -- paired with the transport verb וְהוֹצִיאַ֨נִי֙ 'he brought me out', which makes 42:15 a verse of the counted guided-motion class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences) and gives the onset a licensed driver inside the vision. Four cardinal-direction measurements follow (east 42:16, north 42:17, south 42:18, west 42:19), each carrying its own measure verb, verse-initial at 42:16 and 42:17 and after the direction word at 42:18 and 42:19, then a summary at 42:20. Close side: 42:20 ends on the wall's purpose, לְהַבְדִּ֕יל בֵּ֥ין הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ לְחֹֽל (oshb:Ezek.42.20) “to make a separation between that which was holy and that which was common” (web:Ezek.42.20) -- a genuine thematic close, and the point at which the whole measuring circuit that opened at 40:5 ends, immediately before 43:1's transport verb and the glory's return open a new kind of scene. Both sides of this seam are unusually well aligned: a completion-formula onset and a purpose-clause close on one side, a transport-plus-glory onset on the other.
P10-011.device_notes: No parashah mark stands anywhere in chapter 42 (single-witness); the first mark after the pe at oshb:Ezek.39.29 is the samekh recorded on 43:9, so this seam has no Masoretic paragraph corroboration of its own. One K/Q verse disclosed (42:16): the ketiv reads cubits where the qere reads hundreds, so the disputed word is the multiplier of the reed count itself, a numeral; no boundary is argued from it. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: two occurrences (42:15, 42:20); where each stands within its verse is not recoverable from the verse text of the witness.
